The viewpoint is about 3 metres up, at upper-storey height.

THE PLACE
architectural documentary plate of the sweeping Neoclassical Georgian crescent at Ainslie Place, Edinburgh. Monumental curved facade designed by James Gillespie Graham, constructed from finely dressed pale buff Craigleith ashlar sandstone. Ground floor defined by horizontal channelling, round-arched doorways with radiating fanlights, and timber panelled doors.

STRUCTURE AND MASSING
Typology: Late Georgian / Regency Neoclassical palatial crescent terrace, forming the south-western crescent of Ainslie Place (Moray Estate master plan by James Gillespie Graham, c. Massing & Storeys: Monumental 3-storey plus sunken basement and attic storey block with continuous horizontal continuity.

SURFACES AND MATERIALS
Primary Facade: Dressed Craigleith ashlar sandstone blocks with finely stugged, rusticated ground courses and polished upper courses. Metalwork & Railings: Cast-iron spearhead railings, urn finials, and overthrow lamp arches along front basement drop areas; decorative anthemion-pattern cast-iron balconettes at first-floor sills.
